name: Commit Message
description: A Conventional Commits message: typed subject in the imperative under 72 characters, a body that explains why (not what) wrapped at 72, and the provenance trailer when an AI wrote significant code.

placeholders.name: type
placeholders.description: feat, fix, refactor, perf, docs, test, build, ci, or chore.

placeholders.name: subject
placeholders.description: Imperative mood, no trailing period, subject line ≤ 72 characters including type and scope.
placeholders.example: add template class for rendered documents

placeholders.name: body
placeholders.description: Why this change, the non-obvious decisions, and what alternatives were rejected. Wrap at 72. Omit for trivial changes.
placeholders.example: Agents asked to write an ADR had no skeleton…

placeholders.name: trailers
placeholders.description: Co-Authored-By and similar trailers, one per line.

example:
feat(schemas): add template class for rendered documents

Agents asked to write an ADR, runbook, or handoff had no skeleton to
fill. A template carries the skeleton, its placeholders, and one rendered
example; rendering is a distinct runtime action from injecting text.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rules: Subject line ≤ 72 characters, imperative mood, no trailing period.
One logical change per commit; refactor commits never carry feat or fix payloads.
Body explains why; the diff already says what.

provenance.author: convergent-systems-co
provenance.notes: Rules from the AI Constitution's commit discipline (§4.10.2) and provenance rule (§3.32).
